sources.entry: google-cloud-python - Google Cloud client libraries for Python, published as per-service packages.

summary.one_liner: A monorepo of idiomatic Python client libraries for Google Cloud Platform services, published to PyPI as one package per service.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a catalog page for the google-cloud-python project, which hosts Python client libraries for many Google Cloud and Google API services. Each service is a separate PyPI package, and the README lists them in a table with a release level (stable, preview), a PyPI version badge, and links to API issues and client library issues. The stability section explains the PyPI development status classifiers: Stable (GA, backwards-compatible), Beta (mostly stable), and Alpha (work in progress). It also notes that sub-components with "beta" in the import path, such as google.cloud.language_v1beta2, are treated as preview. The listed packages include core and auth libraries (google-api-core, google-auth, google-cloud-core), plus services such as BigQuery, Bigtable, Pub/Sub, Spanner, Storage, Compute Engine, and Kubernetes Engine. The README is truncated, so the full list of services is not visible here.
use_cases: calling Google Cloud services from Python code
installing only the client for one GCP service such as Storage or Pub/Sub
checking whether a Google Cloud Python library is stable or preview
finding the PyPI package name for a Google Cloud service
reporting bugs against a specific Google Cloud Python client
how_to_run: pip install google-cloud-<service> (install the package for the service you need, per the README's per-service packages)
notable: One PyPI package per Google Cloud service, generated and listed in a single index table
Clear stability tiers: Stable (GA) vs Preview (Beta or Alpha), tied to PyPI development status classifiers
Covers hundreds of services including BigQuery, Spanner, Pub/Sub, Storage, and Merchant API clients
Includes shared libraries such as google-api-core and google-auth used by the other clients
caveats: Install commands are not shown in the visible README text; the table is truncated
Preview libraries may change in backwards-incompatible ways
Components under beta import paths are treated as preview even inside stable packages
keywords: store files in google cloud from python
google cloud client install per service
